kill_fact: No kill fact survived. The attack that came closest was the cost-curve test: the record's headline cost claim quotes the wrong metric, but correcting it makes the company's position WORSE, not better, so it cannot break a bear thesis. Cameco's reported Q2 2026 uranium average unit cost of sales was C$70.81/lb (Q2 2025: C$56.19/lb, +26%), not the C$62.21/lb the record calls 'reported average unit cost of sales'; C$62.21 is the produced-and-purchased cash cost (Q2 2025: C$45.66/lb, +36%). The record stitched the 36% growth rate onto the lower level. On the true metric the realized-vs-cost spread is C$22.32/lb (C$93.13 less C$70.81), not the C$30.92/lb the record's prose implies, and per-pound unit margin compressed year over year (C$24.84 to C$22.32) because realized price rose 15% while cost of sales rose 26%. The sum-of-the-parts already uses ~C$70 costs in the adverse case and ~C$75 in the favorable case, so no valuation level breaks. Every other load-bearing number verifies against the 2026-07-31 filing: TTM revenue C$3,474M, TTM free cash flow C$534M against TTM capex C$386M, TTM diluted EPS C$0.82 (earnings yield 0.60%, i.e. ~168x), free-cash-flow yield 0.85%, ROIC 3.93%, ROE 5.09%, H1 net earnings C$156M vs C$391M (-60%), Q2 EPS C$0.058 vs C$0.74 (-92%), gross margin 21.1% vs 29.3% on revenue -7.2%, cash C$1,113M vs total debt C$1,009M, production 3.9Mlb vs sales 7.1Mlb with 2.8Mlb purchased at C$91.40. Reserve truth verifies: 457Mlb to 433Mlb during 2025, 25Mlb removed by production at Cigar Lake, Inkai and McArthur River with only minor offsetting re-estimates. Contract truth verifies verbatim from the call: >28Mlb/yr committed over five years, market-related floors 'in the high 70s escalated' and ceilings '160 escalated'. Cyclical-peak-cheapness does not apply in the trap direction: no valuation guard is passing here, the record is an explicit price objection with base fair value BELOW market, and the name is absent from the nightly scan (GQ_NO_QUANT_COVERAGE), so no deterministic cheapness screen is carrying it.
corrections: THREE corrections, none fatal, two of which cut against the record's own bear framing. (1) COST METRIC MISLABELLED (load-bearing on this lane's cost-curve test). 'Unit cost of sales rose 36% to C$62.21 per pound' conflates two separate disclosed lines. Reported uranium average unit cost of sales (including depreciation and amortisation) was C$70.81/lb in Q2 2026, up 26% from C$56.19/lb; the produced-and-purchased cash cost was C$62.21/lb, up 36% from C$45.66/lb. The correct cost level is C$8.60/lb HIGHER than stated and the correct growth rate is 10pp LOWER. Direction of the cost-curve drift (up the curve, on a raised full-year guide) is confirmed; the magnitude claim as written is not. No valuation level moves because both sum-of-the-parts cases already assume ~C$70-75 costs. (2) THE GOVERNMENT HAIRCUT IS APPLIED AS A CERTAINTY WHEN IT IS UNVESTED. The record deducts 20% of the US$6.5B above US$17.5B from the base Westinghouse leg as though the US government's participation interest were live. It is not. The 2025-10-28 announcement grants the interest 'once vested', and Grant Isaac on the 2026-07-31 call stated the Department of Commerce partnership 'had two important vesting conditions in it. And the first vesting condition was that it was the responsibility of the Department of Commerce to arrange financing of a minimum $80 billion to support the development of AP1000... That would be the trigger that we would look for under that participation interest.' The record itself concedes the definitive agreements remain unsigned. Applying an unvested contingent claim at 100% understates base fair value. Probability-weighting it at 50% raises the Westinghouse leg from US$25.53 to US$26.27 per share and the base sum from US$59.2 to US$59.9, which on the record's own rounding convention lifts base fair value from US$62 to US$63. The favorable case is unchanged: at a US$45B listing the US$80B financing condition is effectively satisfied by construction, so the full deduction stands. The adverse case is unchanged: at a US$16B listing the value sits below the US$17.5B threshold and no deduction arises either way. (3) THE 'NO CONTRACTED BACKLOG' LIMB IS STALE AS OF THE Q2 2026 FILING. The record argues Westinghouse rests on '91 identified reactor opportunities and at least US$80B of planned investment, neither of which is contracted backlog.' Cameco's Q2 2026 MD&A does disclose Westinghouse contracted backlog and new orders entered: Bernstein's Bob Brackett interrogated those disclosed figures on the 2026-07-31 call, management defined backlog as 'at a point in time of December 31, how much contracted business does Westinghouse have for delivery and revenue recognition in the future', and separately disclosed AP1000 two-pack unit economics of US$14-17B. A filed backlog number therefore exists and the claim that the registration statement will reveal contracted backlog 'for the first time' is wrong. This weakens one supporting limb; it does not touch the multiple argument, which is the load-bearing one. NOT A CORRECTION BUT A STALENESS FLAG FOR THE DIRECTOR: the record's live price of US$94.06 (as-of 2026-08-04) is stale. CCJ traded US$98.18 on 2026-08-11 (market cap US$42.8B), +4.4% since the as-of, on no company-specific news. The gap to the corrected base fair value of US$63 widens from 34% to 36%, so the price objection is stronger now, not weaker.
